questions.skill: Write and solve equations for supplementary and complementary angles
questions.prompt: In the figure, angle ABC is a right angle. A ray splits it into angles of x° and (2x + 15)°. Write and solve an equation for x.
questions.prompt_markup:
In the figure, angle ABC is a right angle. A ray splits it into angles of x° and (2x + 15)°.
Write and solve an equation for x.
questions.correct_answer: The equation x + (2x + 15) = 90 and the answer x = 25
questions.grading_note: Both parts are required: a valid equation and the correct solution. Any valid equation is accepted, but the solution must also be correct.

questions.skill: Prove angle relationships formed by parallel lines and a transversal
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. Prove that angle 2 = angle 7. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. Prove that angle 2 = angle 7. Give a reason for each step.
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Example: angle 2 = angle 6 (corresponding angles, because m and n are parallel); angle 6 = angle 7 (vertical angles); so angle 2 = angle 7 (substitution). Other valid chains are accepted. The conclusion without reasons is not full credit.

figure.description: Parallel lines m (top) and n (bottom) are cut by transversal t, which slants up to the right. At line n the angles are numbered 1 (above, left of t), 2 (above, right of t), 3 (below, left of t), and 4 (below, right of t). At line m the angles are numbered 5, 6, 7, and 8 in the same positions.

questions.skill: Prove angle relationships formed by parallel lines and a transversal
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. Prove that angle 2 + angle 8 = 180°. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. Prove that angle 2 + angle 8 = 180°. Give a reason for each step.
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Example: angle 6 + angle 8 = 180° (they form a linear pair); angle 2 = angle 6 (corresponding angles); so angle 2 + angle 8 = 180° (substitution). Other valid chains are accepted. The conclusion without reasons is not full credit.

questions.skill: Prove angle relationships formed by parallel lines and a transversal
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel and angle 2 = 52°. Find angle 8 and give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup:
In the figure, lines m and n are parallel and angle 2 = 52°.
Find angle 8 and give a reason for each step.
questions.correct_answer: 128°: angle 6 = angle 2 = 52° (corresponding angles), and angle 8 = 180° - 52° = 128° (angles 6 and 8 form a linear pair).
questions.grading_note: Both parts are required: 128° and a valid chain of reasons. A number without reasons is not full credit.
